extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent agents, and receiving Offices involved in filing PCT international applications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for language/translation requirements, correction of defects, incorporation by reference of missing or corrected parts, time limits, fees, and consequences affecting the international filing date under the PCT international phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office language acceptance (Rule 12.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every receiving Office must accept at least one language which is both a language of publication and a language accepted by the International Searching Authority (ISA) competent for international searching of applications filed with that Office; a receiving Office may accept one or more other languages for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A translation of the international application is required when the language in which the international application is filed is a language which is not a language of publication and/or a language accepted by the ISA which is to carry out the international search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation required when filing language not accepted by ISA (Rule 12.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is filed in a language not accepted by the ISA that will carry out the international search, the applicant must furnish to the receiving Office a translation into a language both accepted by that ISA and a language of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any sequence listing language-dependent free text, a translation may be required in a new sequence listing; the applicant may replace the text or, if permitted by the RO, add the translation so the sequence listing contains the free text in two languages (one must be English). (See separate rule for translation of the request.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for translation when filing language not accepted by ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: Translation must be furnished to the receiving Office within one month from the date the international application was received by that Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the RO notifies applicant of the international application number/date and the translation hasn't been furnished, the RO will preferably invite the applicant to furnish translation within one month from receipt or, if not furnished, to furnish it and pay any late fee within one month from invitation or two months from receipt, whichever expires later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal consequence for failing to furnish translation or pay late fee (short-term case)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the RO has invited the applicant to furnish the translation and pay any applicable late furnishing fee and the applicant does not do so within the applicable time limit, the international application will be considered withdrawn and the RO will declare it so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any translation and payment received by the RO before the RO makes the declaration of withdrawal, and before the expiration of 15 months from the priority date, will be considered to have been received before expiration of the applicable time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late furnishing fee amount (translations after 1-month limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The late furnishing fee for translations furnished after the one-month time limit is equal to 25% of the international filing fee referred to in item 1 of the Schedule of Fees, excluding any fee for sheets in excess of 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for abstract/text in drawings (Rule 26.3ter(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the abstract or text matter in the drawings is in a language different from the language of the description and claims, the RO will invite the applicant to furnish a translation of the abstract or drawing text into the language in which the application is to be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No invitation if the abstract/text in the drawings is already in the publication language, or if a translation of the application is required for other reasons and will already be in the publication language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when description and claims are not in a single language (Rules 12.3(c)-(e), 26.3ter(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The PCT requires description and claims to be filed in a language accepted by the receiving Office; if they are not in a single language but all languages used are accepted by the RO, the RO will invite the applicant to furnish a translation to provide description and claims in a single language within one month from receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The single language must (i) be one of the languages used as filed; (ii) be accepted by the ISA that will carry out the search; and (iii) be the language of publication. The RO may refrain from inviting a translation if multiple languages assist comprehension (e.g., language-neutral terms, certain technical terms, citations, or translation-technology inventions). If the three criteria cannot be satisfied, the RO invites the applicant to furnish a translation under Rule 12.3 or 12.4. Time limits and late fees apply as described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request must be in a language of publication accepted for filing the request (Rules 12.1(c), 26.3ter(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever the language of the description and claims, the request must always be filed in a language of publication accepted by the receiving Office for filing the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request is not in such a language, the RO invites the applicant to file a complying translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement when filed language accepted by ISA but not a language of publication (Rules 12.4, 48.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application is filed in a language accepted by the ISA but not a language of publication, the applicant must furnish to the RO a translation into a language of publication accepted by that RO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For sequence listings, a translation of language-dependent free text may be required in a new sequence listing. See paragraph references for translation of the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for translation when filed language accepted by ISA but not publication language
rubrics_metrics.description: The translation must be furnished to the RO within 14 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not furnished within that time, the RO will invite the applicant to furnish the translation and to pay any applicable late fee within 16 months from the priority date. Failure to comply may lead to withdrawal, but translations/payments received before the RO's declaration of withdrawal and before 17 months from priority date will be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late furnishing fee amount (translations after 14-month limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The late furnishing fee for translations furnished after the 14-month from priority-date time limit equals 25% of the international filing fee referred to in item 1 of the Schedule of Fees, excluding any fee for sheets in excess of 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defects that influence the international filing date (Article 11(1) / Rule 20 series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain defects will cause the RO to invite correction and may affect the accorded international filing date if not corrected: (i) applicant lacks right to file with that RO because of residence/nationality; (ii) application lacks indication it is intended as international; (iii) missing request designating all Contracting States; (iv) missing name of applicant or minimum name indications; (v) lack on the face of a part appearing to be a description and a part appearing to be a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RO invites correction; time limit for filing the correction is two months from invitation. If correction is made within time limit, date of receipt of the correction becomes the international filing date; otherwise the application is not treated as an international application. For certain defects, the RO will invite confirmation of incorporation by reference under Rule 20.6 to retain an earlier date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defects consisting of missing or erroneously filed parts (Article 14(2) / Rule 20.5 series)
rubrics_metrics.description: If parts of the description, claims, drawings or parts thereof are missing or appear erroneously filed, the RO notifies the applicant and invites correction or confirmation of incorporation by reference. The time limit for furnishing missing parts or correct elements is two months from the date of invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If missing parts or correct elements are furnished within the time limit, the date of their receipt becomes the international filing date unless incorporation by reference is confirmed and retains earlier date. If missing drawings referred to are not furnished within the time limit, references to drawings are considered non-existent and the original filing date remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt of additional sheets on different days (Rule 20.3/20.5 series)
rubrics_metrics.description: If all sheets are not received the same day, receipt of further sheets after an invitation to correct generally results in the date of receipt of those further sheets being accorded as the international filing date, provided they are received within the applicable time limit under Rule 20.7 and incorporation by reference is not used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no invitation was sent and papers completing the application are not received the same day, the RO marks the request with the date on which the papers completing the application were received; that later date is accorded as the filing date if later sheets were received within two months from first receipt. Each sheet is marked with the actual date received. Absence or late receipt of the abstract alone does not, by itself, change the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting incorporation by reference of missing/correct elements (Rule 4.18, 20.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing or correct elements or parts may be incorporated by reference into the international application where the missing/ correct element is completely contained in an earlier application of which priority is claimed as of the date when one or more Article 11(1)(iii) elements were first received by the RO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation by reference will have the effect that the incorporated elements are considered received on the earlier date (so the international filing date can be retained), subject to compatibility notifications by ROs under Rule 20.8. If incorporation is needed after filing, applicant may request transmission to the IB as RO under Rule 19.4(a)(iii) which accepts incorporation by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for the statement and confirmation of incorporation by reference (Rule 4.18, 20.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of incorporation by reference must have been included in the international application on the date when one or more Article 11(1)(iii) elements were first received (Form PCT/RO/101 includes it automatically). If the statement was not contained in the request at filing, it can only be added if it was otherwise contained in or submitted with the application at filing. One or several priority claims that completely contain the missing/correct element must have been made at filing; adding such priority claims later is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must confirm incorporation by written notice to the RO within the applicable time limit and attach: the sheet(s) embodying the entire element/part as contained in the earlier application; a copy of the earlier application if Rule 17.1 requirements not complied with; any required translations; and, for missing/correct parts, an indication where the part is in the earlier application and translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for confirming incorporation by reference (Rule 20.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no invitation was sent, the time limit to confirm is two months from the date on which papers were first received by the RO; where an invitation was issued, the time limit is two months from the date of mailing of the invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this time limit expires after the expiration of 12 months from the filing date of the earliest application whose priority is claimed, the RO will warn the applicant that failure to confirm may lead to loss of priority; corrections/notices received after the two-month limit but before the RO sends its Rule 20.4(i) notification are considered timely (Rule 20.7(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of erroneously filed elements when incorporation confirmed (Rule 20.5bis(d), Section 309(b)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a correct element/part is considered to have been contained in the purported international application on the date when Article 11(1)(iii) elements were first received under Rule 20.6(b), the erroneously filed element/part will remain in the application but will be marked 'ERRONEOUSLY FILED (RULE 20.5bis)' and moved to the end of the corresponding element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RO will transmit the erroneously filed sheets to the International Bureau and they will be published as part of the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if incorporation by reference requirements not complied with
rubrics_metrics.description: If not all requirements for incorporation by reference are fulfilled (e.g., the missing/correct element is not entirely contained in the earlier application), the international application will be assigned a later international filing date equal to the date of receipt of the missing/correct element to the extent other Article 11(1) requirements are met on that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant may request that the missing/correct part be disregarded under Rule 20.5(e) or 20.5bis(e); if disregarded, the earlier filing date will be reinstated and the submitted part considered not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of successful incorporation by reference on designated/elected Offices (Rule 20.8(c), Rule 82ter.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: In most Contracting States, incorporated elements/parts will be treated as if they had been contained in the international application as originally filed. Designated/elected Offices may review RO decisions allowing incorporation under Rule 82ter.1(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a designated/elected Office finds failures (missing priority document; missing statement of incorporation; no written notice; no required translation; element not completely contained in priority document), it may treat the application as if the filing date were the date on which the sheets containing the elements were submitted, but only after giving the applicant an opportunity to make observations and/or request disregard. Offices that have notified incompatibility under Rule 20.8(b)/(b-bis) may treat the application differently, with similar procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defects that do not influence the international filing date (Article 14(1), Rule 26 series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain defects do not affect the accorded international filing date and the RO will invite correction: (i) application not signed (or lacks seal where applicable); (ii) applicant name not presented in prescribed way (other than specified exceptions); (iii) no title; (iv) no abstract; (v) physical requirements non-compliance to the extent necessary for reasonably uniform publication; (vi) any element other than description and claims not in an admitted language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RO invites correction with a two-month time limit; if corrected within the time limit (including any extension), the international filing date remains the original date; otherwise the application is considered withdrawn. Note some Offices have notified incompatibility with Rule 26.3ter(a) so all elements may need to comply with language requirements before a filing date is accorded at those Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing in a language not accepted by the receiving Office — transmittal to International Bureau (Rule 19.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is filed in a language not accepted by the national/regional Office but accepted by the International Bureau as receiving Office, the national/regional Office will consider it received on behalf of the IB and promptly transmit it to the IB (the IB accepts applications filed in any language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The national/regional Office will date-stamp and transmit the application (subject to national security). Transmittal may require a transmittal fee; other fees paid will be refunded by the national/regional Office and then paid to the IB. The application is considered received by the IB on the date received by the national/regional Office, but for calculating time limits for paying fees due on filing, the date of receipt is when the IB actually receives the application.
